key_insight: Non-binary detector error models preserve Pauli fault distributions exactly while enabling smaller decoding graphs and better belief-propagation performance than binary models.
engineering_relevance: Tanner graphs with 4–5× fewer edges can reduce decoder connectivity demands, while BP with OSD achieved up to 9.4× CPU speedup.
method: Represent each circuit fault location as one random variable over its original Pauli-error alphabet.
Use split-merge-regroup to compact Clifford-circuit models by merging components with identical detector and observable effects.
Decode using belief propagation with one scalar message per edge, optionally followed by OSD.
evidence_signal: Numerical evaluations on surface, color, and bivariate bicycle codes report better BP performance with and without OSD, fewer graph edges, and faster CPU decoding.
watch_item: The reported speedup is a best-case CPU result; hardware latency and resource savings require implementation-specific validation.
